title: Elora washroom garbage plan deferred; termite subsidy advances
subtitle: Elora BIA loan, attainable housing referral, hydro debt agreement, green space donation and museum liquor exemption also considered.
overview: Council deferred a decision on the Tourism Washroom Project Update to September 30 so staff can answer questions raised at the meeting. The proposal would add Molok garbage containers beside the planned East Mill Street washrooms in downtown Elora. The Elora BIA supported it, while nearby property owners said they had not been consulted and asked for another location {{vote:m11}}.

Council directed staff to develop a subsidy-style termite management program and to sign preferred-pricing agreements with two pest control firms. Staff will return with a formal program and the vendors' communications plans {{vote:m13}}. Council also approved a $50,000 interest-free loan to the Elora BIA for replacement downtown Christmas light features {{vote:m7}}, and referred a proposal on attainable housing to staff for a report after budget season {{vote:m3}}.

Other approvals included a Green Space donation agreement for Elora improvements {{vote:m12}}, a Centre Wellington Hydro subordination agreement tied to new debt for substation work {{vote:m9}}, and a letter seeking a liquor licensing exemption for the County Museum and Archives lands {{vote:m6}}. Nothing was reported from the closed session on a possible land acquisition.

decisions.item: Tourism washroom project and Molok containers
decisions.detail: Council deferred Report CS2024-27 to the September 30 meeting so staff can provide more information and answer questions raised at this meeting.
Staff will develop a subsidy-style program, sign agreements with Aetna Pest Control Ltd. and Orkin Canada for services and preferred pricing, and bring a formal program back to Council.
Council approved by-laws amending the BIA borrowing rights and providing a $50,000 interest-free loan to buy replacement downtown Christmas light features.
A delegate's proposal for municipally led attainable housing was referred to staff for review, with a report back after this year's budget season.

The Mayor and Clerk may sign the donation agreement with Kat Florence Canada Corporation Ltd., and the Managing Director of Community Services may approve design, timing and budget changes and contracts.

The Mayor and Clerk may sign a subordination agreement with Ontario Infrastructure and Lands Corporation to secure new debt for the Elora EMS-2 transformer replacement and the Fergus FMS-5 distribution station.

decisions.item: Liquor licence exemption for County museum
decisions.detail: Staff will facilitate a letter asking the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario for a property exemption regulation for the Wellington County Museum & Archives lands.
Council received the 2024 progress report and directed staff to prepare a 2025 Corporate Business Plan alongside the 2025 budget.
